Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which organization, club or musical group is Dominique Villars a member of?
Document 1: Here is a Wikipedia-style entry that presents comprehensive evidence for the statement:

**Dominique Villars**

Dominique Villars (1745-1814) was a French botanist and lichenologist who made significant contributions to the field of botany, particularly in the study of lichens. **Membership in the Academy of Sciences of Turin**

Villars was a member of the Academy of Sciences of Turin, a prestigious science academy founded in 1757 in Turin, Italy. This membership is a testament to Villars' reputation as a prominent botanist of his time. **Evidence**

Several credible sources confirm Villars' membership in the Academy of Sciences of Turin:

* The Academy of Sciences of Turin's own records list Villars as a member. According to the Academy's archives, Villars was elected as a foreign member in 1786. [1]
* The French National Library's catalog of scientific publications includes a reference to Villars' membership in the Academy of Sciences of Turin. [2]
* A biography of Villars published in the journal "Annales des Sciences Naturelles" in 1815 also mentions his membership in the Academy of Sciences of Turin. [3]
* The "Biographie Universelle" by Louis-Gabriel Michaud, a comprehensive biographical dictionary published in the 19th century, lists Villars as a member of the Academy of Sciences of Turin. [4]

**References**

[1] Academy of Sciences of Turin. (1786). Archives of the Academy of Sciences of Turin. [2] Bibliothèque nationale de France. (n.d.). Catalogue général. Retrieved from <https:\/\/catalogue.bnf.fr\/>

[3] "Annales des Sciences Naturelles". (1815). Vol. 6, p. 345. [4] Michaud, L.-G. (1843). Biographie Universelle. Vol. 43, p. 567.
Document 2: **RENOWNED FRENCH BOTANIST DOMINIQUE VILLARS INDUCTED INTO PRESTIGIOUS ACADEMIA EUROPAEA**

Paris, France - In a ceremony held at the historic Sorbonne University, French botanist and lichenologist Dominique Villars was officially inducted into the esteemed Academia Europaea, a pan-European academy dedicated to promoting excellence in scientific research and education. Villars, a pioneer in the field of lichenology, was recognized for his groundbreaking contributions to the study of lichens, including the discovery of several new species and the development of innovative classification methods. His work has had a profound impact on the scientific community, inspiring a new generation of researchers to explore the fascinating world of lichens. "I am deeply honored to be part of this prestigious academy," Villars said in an exclusive interview. "It is a testament to the tireless efforts of my colleagues and me to advance our understanding of the natural world. I look forward to collaborating with fellow members to push the boundaries of scientific knowledge." The Academia Europaea, founded in 1988, is a leading institution that brings together top scholars from across Europe to promote interdisciplinary research and exchange. With over 4,000 members from more than 70 countries, the academy is a hub for intellectual excellence and innovation. "Dr. Villars' induction is a significant milestone for our academy," said Professor Maria Teresa Lago, President of the Academia Europaea. "His remarkable achievements in botany and lichenology embody the spirit of scientific inquiry and collaboration that our institution embodies. We are thrilled to welcome him to our community of distinguished scholars." According to data from the Academia Europaea, Villars is one of only 15 French scientists to be inducted into the academy since its inception. His membership is a testament to France's rich tradition of scientific excellence and its continued contribution to the global scientific community. Villars' research has been widely published in leading scientific journals, including the Journal of Lichenology and the Annales des Sciences Naturelles. His work has also been recognized by the French Academy of Sciences, which awarded him the prestigious Prix de Coincy in 1803. As a member of the Academia Europaea, Villars will participate in high-level scientific discussions, contribute to policy debates, and collaborate with fellow members on cutting-edge research projects.
